Plot where an incomplete trajectory's papers go (variable-width lines)

Source: R/plot_trajectory_destination.R
plot_trajectory_destination.Rd

Renders the destinations of a stagnant trajectory in the same visual idiom as plot_group_trajectories_lines_2d(): a Sugiyama time layout (year on the x-axis) with one variable-width line per destination, so the reader follows the cohort left to right as a continuation of the 2d/3d trajectory plots. Each line tracks, year by year, the group that holds most of that destination's papers; line width grows with the number of papers carried.

Usage

plot_trajectory_destination(
  destination,
  color_by = c("group", "trajectory"),
  min_prop = 0,
  title = NULL,
  width_range = c(0.8, 7),
  show_only_highlighted = FALSE,
  label_size = 4,
  lowlight_color = "#9AA5B1",
  lowlight_alpha = 0.25,
  lowlight_width = 0.6
)

Arguments

destination

Output of sniff_trajectory_destination() (must contain a flow tibble; color_by = "trajectory" additionally needs the dest_traj column produced when all_detected was supplied).

color_by

Colour the lines by destination "group" (default) or by destination "trajectory".

min_prop

Destinations capturing less than min_prop of the cohort are merged into a single grey (other) line (default: 0, keep all).

title

Plot title. Defaults to a summary of the terminal node and the dominant continuation.

width_range

Range for line widths, scaled by papers carried (default: c(0.8, 7)).

show_only_highlighted

Hide the grey background skeleton, drawing only the destination lines (default: FALSE).

label_size

Text size for the end labels (default: 4).

lowlight_color, lowlight_alpha, lowlight_width

Style of the background skeleton edges.

Value

A ggplot object.

See also

sniff_trajectory_destination(), plot_trajectory_handoff(), plot_group_trajectories_lines_2d()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
detected <- detect_main_trajectories(groups_cumulative_trajectories, "c1g10")
dest <- sniff_trajectory_destination(
  detected, "tr3", groups_cumulative_trajectories$docs_per_group,
  all_detected = groups_detected_trajectories, group = "c1g10"
)
plot_trajectory_destination(dest, color_by = "trajectory", min_prop = 0.03)
} # }
